title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Putting Withdrawn Coverage Back in Force
content:
## Credit control desk entry

Where coverage on a Preventive Maintenance Agreements record has been withdrawn, it may be put back in force and charged for. The charge for putting coverage back in force is worked out only after the arrears standing on the agreement are answered by a payment recorded against the agreement as a whole rather than against any named invoice.

### What the entry does

The agreement moves out of its withdrawn standing and back into the renewal window it was withdrawn from, today is stamped as the day coverage was restored, the charge for restoring it is booked against the agreement, and the amount the owner owes is raised by that charge. Afterwards visits may be booked again on the agreement, the charge appears in its history and its outstanding balance is higher by exactly the charge booked.

### How it is recorded

The desk unlocks the agent-side tool `reinstate_agreement_coverage_5877576a` and calls it. One call restores the coverage and books the charge together.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `agreement_id` | the reference number of the preventive maintenance agreement record whose coverage is restored | an identifier, read from the maintenance agreement lookup before the call |
| `reinstatement_charge_usd` | the money amount charged for restoring coverage | USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half up at the cent; an amount of zero is accepted and books a zero charge |

### Return

The call returns a one-line confirmation naming the agreement restored, the standing it now carries, the reference number of the charge entry created and the amount charged in USD to two decimal places. That line is issued only when the standing has been changed, the charge written and the outstanding balance raised; it is the receipt of completion.
